title: Rapid, direct, and sensitive determination of aziridine and 2-chloroethylamine by hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
author: Shackman
materials: AZ (1 g/L in methanol) was from SPEX CertiPrep (Metuchen, NJ, USA). 99% CEA, HPLC gradient grade acetonitrile, > 99.995% ammonium formate, ACS reagent grade GLY, and >99% L-phenylalanine (PHE) were from Sigma-Aldrich (St. Louis, MO, USA). Water was purified in-house using an Advantage A10 purification system (Millipore Sigma, Burlington, MA, USA). ASV potassium salt was from Bristol-Myers Squibb (New Brunswick, NJ, USA). All samples and standards were prepared in an ammonium formate (0.1 M) : acetonitrile (5 : 95, v/v) diluent; pH was unadjusted. All standards had both analytes of interest (AZ and CEA) present together. Samples were directly weighed into 1.7 mL polypropylene centrifuge tubes (VWR, Radnor, PA, USA), diluted to either 50 or 100 g/L by autopipette, vortexed for 30 s (Vortex Genie 2, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc., Waltham, MA, USA) to a uniform solution or slurry, and centrifuged at 14,000 RPM for 1 min (5415C, Eppendorf, Hauppauge, NY, USA). The supernatant (if undissolved material remained) was transferred to an HPLC vial for analysis.

steps.title: Prepare diluent and reagents
steps.instruction: Make the diluent by mixing 0.1 M ammonium formate with acetonitrile in a 5 : 95 (v/v) ratio; pH is left unadjusted. Gather AZ stock (1 g/L in methanol, SPEX CertiPrep), CEA (99 % purity), GLY (ACS grade), L‑phenylalanine (>99 %), ASV potassium salt, and HPLC‑grade water (in‑house purified).

steps.title: Weigh, dilute, vortex, and centrifuge samples
steps.instruction: For each sample, weigh the required amount directly into a 1.7 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube (VWR). Dilute with the prepared diluent to a final concentration of either 50 g/L or 100 g/L using an autopipette. Vortex the tube for 30 seconds with a Vortex Genie 2 to obtain a uniform solution or slurry, then centrifuge at 14 000 RPM for 1 minute using an Eppendorf 5415C.

substeps.instruction: Weigh sample into 1.7 mL PP tube.
Add diluent to reach 50 g/L or 100 g/L.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to HPLC vial
steps.instruction: If any undissolved material remains after centrifugation, carefully pipette the clear supernatant into an HPLC vial for subsequent analysis.

steps.title: Set up HILIC‑MS system
steps.instruction: Install a 5 cm UHPLC column (sub‑2 µm particle size, BEH stationary phase). Configure the system for an isocratic run using the same diluent as mobile phase, with a total run time of 1.5 min (retention factor ≈ 4 for AZ). Use the benchtop mass spectrometer’s default tuning parameters for high eluent flow rates; no further tuning is required. Verify that no interfering peaks appear in the AZ (44.1 m/z) or CEA (79.9 m/z) SIM channels.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards and inject
steps.instruction: Create calibration standards containing both AZ and CEA at equal concentrations ranging from 0.5 µg/L to 10 µg/L in the diluent. Inject each concentration in triplicate. Confirm linearity (R² > 0.99), signal‑to‑noise (≥ 22 for CEA, ≥ 4 for AZ at 0.5 µg/L), and injection precision (3 % RSD for CEA, 10 % RSD for AZ at low levels; < 1 % RSD for both at ≥ 2 µg/L).

steps.title: Perform spike‑and‑recovery tests
steps.instruction: For each matrix (GLY, PHE, ASV), weigh the matrix into a tube and dilute to 100 g/L (or 50 g/L for ASV in the second set). Spike with AZ and CEA standards to achieve a target of 50 ppb (add 5 µg/L standards for the 100 g/L matrix; add 2.5 µg/L standards for the 50 g/L ASV matrix). Process the spiked samples as described in steps 2–3, then analyze by HILIC‑MS. Calculate recovery and repeatability; expect < 4 % RSD and recovery within 5 % for GLY and PHE, and within 10 % for ASV after the concentration adjustment.

substeps.instruction: Prepare matrix at 100 g/L (GLY, PHE, ASV) or 50 g/L (ASV).
Spike with 5 µg/L (or 2.5 µg/L for 50 g/L ASV) to reach 50 ppb.
Analyze by HILIC‑MS and compute recovery/RSD.
